name: Capacity and server use
answer: These measures show how much of a facility's power and space servers actually use, and how much sits stranded. For AI buildings the question is whether expensive capacity is earning, because idle accelerators and stranded power are paid for either way.

metrics.line: The share of provisioned compute doing real work, measured over time rather than at peak.
metrics.label: Server utilization rate

metrics.line: Utility power or floor space that is allocated and paid for but cannot be used, because the other of the pair ran out first or airflow limits were reached.
metrics.label: Stranded power and space per cabinet

metrics.line: The structural weight the raised floor or slab supports per square foot, against the actual weight of installed racks.
metrics.label: Floor loading limits

reading.body:
Utilization, stranded capacity, and floor loading decide whether a data center's power and space are actually earning, and idle capacity is paid for either way.

The three measures describe the same gap from different sides. Utilization is the share of provisioned compute doing real work, measured over time rather than at peak. Stranded power and space is capacity that is allocated and paid for but unusable, because the paired resource ran out first or airflow limits were reached. Floor loading is the structural weight a raised floor or slab supports per square foot against the weight of installed racks. Each one asks whether capacity that exists can be used.

For AI buildings this matters because accelerators and the power behind them are expensive whether or not they run. A facility can hold provisioned power and still strand it if cooling or airflow runs out first, and it can hold floor space that racks cannot occupy because the slab will not carry them. Utilization measured over time rather than at peak is the honest version of the number, since peak tells you what the building can do and the time series tells you what it did.

The data covers what these measures mean and not what any facility reports. It gives no utilization figures, no stranded capacity rates, no floor loading values, and no comparison across operators or regions. A reader should treat it as a definition of the terms, not as evidence about how much capacity is idle in practice.
